messages.subject: plotting support values for midpoint rooted tree using geom_nodepoint after conversion to `phylo` and `treedata` object
messages.subject_clean: plotting support values for midpoint rooted tree using geom_nodepoint after conversion to `phylo` and `treedata` object
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I would like to draw a midpoint-rooted tree with node support values. I have my data in newick format. See minimal working example.

## MWE

library(treeio)
library(ggtree)
library(ggplot2)
library(ape)
library(phangorn)
tree_td <- treeio::read.newick("booster_
sdi_1000.nw", node.label = "support")
ggtree(tree_td) + geom_nodepoint(aes(color = support)) + scale_color_continuous(low = "red", high = "green")

## midpoint rooting --> convert treedata to phylo object
tree_p <- as.phylo(tree_td)
tree_p <-midpoint(tree_p)
tree_p
## tree_p does not have support feature --> converting back to `treedata` object

tree_td_2 <- as.treedata(tree_p)
tree_td_2@data
tree_td@data

## end MWE

The problem is, that after converting from `treedata` object to `phylo` object the information on support values is lost.
Further complication is that the topology of the tree changed due to the midpoint rooting, thus a simple `tree_td_2@data <- tree_td@data` does not really work.

I am wondering, if there is a way to plot a midpoint rooted tree with its support values as nodepoints?

Many thanks and best,
Thomas

messages.subject_clean: Highliting or indicating specific sites in msa plot
messages.body_plain:
Hello!
I'm wondering if there is a way to highlight or point to specific sites of interest in a multiple sequence alignment plot. For instance, I have an msa plot next to a phylogeny and I'm trying to highlight or indicate the specific sites of functional divergence between clades in the msa plot. I would just need to circle them or point the sites in the alignment. I'm using ggtree.

Best regards!!!

messages.subject_clean: To truncate the highest bar in the plot
messages.body_plain:
I would recommend you to plot each panel separately. You can figure out a way to plot truncated bar in ggplot2 (or other specific needs that are not supported in ggtree directly).

Then you can put them together based on the trick mentioned in https://yulab-smu.github.io/treedata-book/chapter7.html#composite_plot.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Dr. Yu,

I'm trying to utilise the function ggdensitree with scripts as followed, and got the error message "could not find function "ggdensitree." May I know if this function is still working or it's no longer there please? I'm using ggtree v1.16.6 and R v3.6.3.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
btrees <- read.tree(system.file("extdata/RAxML", "RAxML_bootstrap.H3", package="treeio"))
ggtree(btrees) + facet_wrap(~.id, ncol=10)

ggdensitree(btrees, alpha=.3, colour='steelblue') +
    geom_tiplab(size=3) + xlim(0, 45)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Thank you for your kind support and help.

Best,

Peiyu
